title: Formalism and Reader-Response
text:
Formalist criticism treats a literary work as a self-contained object, whose meaning arises from the interplay of its formal elements rather than from the author's biography. Its proponents argued that imposing extrinsic historical or psychological readings obscures the text's intrinsic coherence. Such an approach, however, tends to sideline the reader, whose role in producing meaning becomes marginal.

Reader-response theory, by contrast, locates meaning in the encounter between text and reader. Critics in this tradition contend that every reading is shaped by the interpretive conventions a reader brings, so no interpretation can claim absolute authority. Nevertheless, proponents insist that this openness does not dissolve the text entirely, since it still constrains the range of plausible readings.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do formalist critics consider the source of a work's meaning?
options: The author's biography and historical context
The interplay of the work's formal elements

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do reader-response critics contend about interpretation?
options: Every reading is shaped by the reader's interpretive conventions
Only the author can give a definitive interpretation
Texts have one fixed meaning that all readers recognise
Readings are unrelated to the text itself

questions.text: What can be inferred about the formalists' view of historical readings?
options: They consider such readings essential to understanding the text
They regard such readings as potentially distorting the text's coherence
They believe historical readings are always accurate
They think historical readings should replace formal analysis entirely

questions.text: Why do the proponents of reader-response theory insist that openness does not dissolve the text entirely?
options: To argue that texts play no role at all
To prevent the position from collapsing into unlimited relativism
To suggest that authors should be consulted
To return to the formalist view of meaning

paragraph_translations: Krytyka formalistyczna traktuje dzieło literackie jako samodzielny obiekt, którego znaczenie wynika ze wzajemnego oddziaływania jego elementów formalnych, a nie z biografii autora. Jej zwolennicy twierdzili, że narzucanie zewnętrznych, historycznych lub psychologicznych interpretacji przesłania wewnętrzną spójność tekstu. Takie podejście jednak zwykle marginalizuje czytelnika, którego rola w tworzeniu znaczenia staje się drugorzędna.

Teoria recepcji natomiast umieszcza znaczenie w spotkaniu tekstu z czytelnikiem. Krytycy z tego nurtu twierdzą, że każda interpretacja jest kształtowana przez konwencje interpretacyjne, które czytelnik wnosi do lektury, więc żadna interpretacja nie może pretendować do absolutnego autorytetu. Zwolennicy tej teorii podkreślają jednak, że ta otwartość nie rozpuszcza tekstu całkowicie, ponieważ wciąż ogranicza zakres prawdopodobnych odczytań.
